name: MI-11
label: Likely D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by nine points and the cycle's environment favors Democrats
Jeremy Moss holds a roughly 13-to-1 fundraising edge over Ethan Baker, plus outside support
Open seat removes incumbency and is the main source of added uncertainty
Prediction markets price Democratic odds near 95 percent
model.rationale: The forecast rests on a Democratic-leaning district and a favorable environment, reinforced by Moss's overwhelming fundraising advantage; the open seat, a well-funded independent, and the absence of polling add uncertainty but not enough to move the race out of Safe Democratic territory.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or an unexpectedly strong independent showing could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Haley Stevens (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Democrats defend an open seat in a district that leaned Democratic by nine points at the presidential level. Haley Stevens is leaving for a Senate run, so neither major party has an incumbent on the ballot. Jeremy Moss enters the general as a heavy fundraiser, having raised about $1.8 million to Republican Ethan Baker's roughly $142,000, and outside groups have added support on the Democratic side. An independent, Anil Kumar, has also raised a notable sum.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals. Prediction markets put Democratic odds around 95 percent. The combination of a Democratic-leaning electorate, a favorable environment, and a large money edge points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the open seat the main source of uncertainty.
